records.source: מַשָּׂ֖א גֵּ֣יא חִזָּי֑וֹן מַה־לָּ֣ךְ אֵפ֔וֹא כִּֽי־עָלִ֥ית כֻּלָּ֖ךְ לַגַּגּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: [The] oracle of [the] valley of vision. What [is] to you now, that you have gone up, all of you, to the roofs,
pieces: An oracle about the valley of vision. \q What is wrong with you now, \q that all of you have climbed up onto the roofs?

L.1: The oracle [concerning] the valley of vision. \q What [is the matter] with you now, \q that you have gone up, all of you, to the roofs?

R.1: This is a message about the valley of vision, that is, Jerusalem. \q What is happening to you, people of Jerusalem? \q Why have all of you gone up onto your flat roofs?

decisions.choice: oracle: a solemn message from God announced against a place
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to lift up" and heads each of the oracles about the nations in chapters 13-23 (see the note at 13:1). In 22:25 the same word means a load hung on a peg.

decisions.choice: the valley of vision: Jerusalem, the place where the prophet saw his visions
alternatives: a valley near Jerusalem where a vision came
decisions.reason: The oracles before this one are about foreign nations, but verses 8-11 name Judah, the city of David and Jerusalem. Jerusalem sits on hills ringed by valleys (verse 7); the name may be ironic, since the city that received visions did not see (verse 11).

decisions.choice: to the roofs: up onto the flat roofs of the houses
decisions.reason: Houses had flat roofs used for living and work. The people climb up to watch, whether to celebrate (verse 2) or to see the enemy (verses 6-7).

decisions.choice: message
decisions.reason: As at 13:1, Readable says "message"; Literal and Balanced say "oracle".

decisions.choice: that is, Jerusalem / people of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable names the city that verses 9-10 identify, so the reader knows who is addressed.

records.heading: The valley of vision

records.source: תְּשֻׁא֣וֹת׀מְלֵאָ֗ה עִ֚יר הֽוֹמִיָּ֔ה קִרְיָ֖ה עַלִּיזָ֑ה חֲלָלַ֨יִךְ֙ לֹ֣א חַלְלֵי־חֶ֔רֶב וְלֹ֖א מֵתֵ֥י מִלְחָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: noises full, city turbulent, town exultant, your slain [are] not slain of [the] sword, and not dead of battle.
pieces: You are full of shouting, a city in uproar, a town in high spirits. \q Your dead were not cut down by the sword or killed in battle.

L.2: [You who are] full of noises, turbulent city, exultant town, \q your slain [are] not slain by [the] sword, and not dead in battle.

R.2: The whole city is noisy and wild with excitement. \q But your people who have died were not killed by swords. They did not die fighting in a battle.

decisions.choice: full of noises ... exultant town: a city of loud, careless celebration
decisions.reason: The same words describe Tyre (23:7) and a proud city brought low (32:13). The city rejoices while disaster is coming (verse 13).

decisions.choice: your slain not slain by the sword: your dead did not die fighting
alternatives: your dead died of famine and disease
decisions.reason: The word for "slain" usually means someone pierced in battle. Here the dead did not fall in combat; the next verse suggests they were caught fleeing, and siege also brought death by hunger and disease (Lamentations 4:9).

decisions.choice: noisy and wild with excitement
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the three titles of the city describe.

records.source: כָּל־קְצִינַ֥יִךְ נָֽדְדוּ־יַ֖חַד מִקֶּ֣שֶׁת אֻסָּ֑רוּ כָּל־נִמְצָאַ֨יִךְ֙ אֻסְּר֣וּ יַחְדָּ֔ו מֵרָח֖וֹק בָּרָֽחוּ׃
records.gloss: All your rulers have fled together; without [the] bow they have been captured; all [those] found in you were captured together; from afar they had fled.
pieces: All your leaders ran away together and were taken prisoner without a bow being drawn. \q All of you who were found were captured together, though they had fled far away.

L.3: All your rulers have fled together; without [a] bow they have been captured. \q All [those] found in you were captured together; far away they had fled.

R.3: All your leaders ran away together. They were captured without a fight. \q Everyone who was found was taken prisoner, even those who had run far away.

decisions.choice: without the bow: captured without a shot being fired
decisions.reason: The preposition can mean "from" or "without". The leaders surrendered without fighting. It may instead mean "by the bowmen", captured by archers.

decisions.choice: your rulers have fled: the leaders desert the city
decisions.reason: When Babylon broke into Jerusalem in 587/586 BC, King Zedekiah and his soldiers fled by night and were captured near Jericho (2 Kings 25:4-6). Whether Isaiah sees that event or a similar flight in 701 BC, the leaders' flight is part of the city's shame.

decisions.choice: without a fight
decisions.reason: Readable explains "without a bow".

records.source: עַל־כֵּ֥ן אָמַ֛רְתִּי שְׁע֥וּ מִנִּ֖י אֲמָרֵ֣ר בַּבֶּ֑כִי אַל־תָּאִ֣יצוּ לְנַֽחֲמֵ֔נִי עַל־שֹׁ֖ד בַּת־עַמִּֽי׃
records.gloss: Therefore I said, look away from me; I will be bitter in weeping; do not hasten to comfort me over [the] destruction of [the] daughter of my people.
pieces: So I said, "Turn your eyes away from me; leave me to my bitter weeping. \q Do not rush to comfort me \q for the ruin of the daughter of my people."

L.4: Therefore I said, "Look away from me; I will be bitter in weeping. \q Do not hurry to comfort me \q over the destruction of the daughter of my people."

R.4: So I said, "Leave me alone, and let me cry hard. \q Do not try to comfort me. \q My people have been destroyed."

decisions.choice: the daughter of my people: my people, spoken of tenderly
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures the people as a beloved daughter. Jeremiah uses it often in his laments over Jerusalem (Jeremiah 8:21-22; 9:1).

decisions.choice: I said: the prophet speaks for himself
decisions.reason: The prophet's own grief breaks into the oracle. It stands against the city's celebration in verses 2 and 13.

decisions.choice: my people
decisions.reason: Readable drops the picture of a daughter and says "my people"; Literal and Balanced keep it.

records.source: כִּ֣י יוֹם֩ מְהוּמָ֨ה וּמְבוּסָ֜ה וּמְבוּכָ֗ה לַֽאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת בְּגֵ֣יא חִזָּי֑וֹן מְקַרְקַ֥ר קִ֖ר וְשׁ֥וֹעַ אֶל־הָהָֽר׃
records.gloss: For a day of panic and trampling and confusion [belongs] to [the] Lord Yahweh of hosts in [the] valley of vision, breaking down [the] wall and crying out to the mountain.
pieces: For the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies brings a day of panic and trampling and confusion to the valley of vision, \q a day when walls are broken through and cries ring out toward the mountain.

L.5: For [it is] a day of panic and trampling and confusion [belonging] to the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of hosts in the valley of vision, \q a breaking down of [the] wall and a crying out to the mountain.

R.5: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies has chosen a day when people in the valley of vision will panic. They will be trampled and confused. \q Enemies will break down the city walls. People will scream for help toward the hills.

decisions.choice: a day ... belonging to the Lord: a day of the Lord's judgment
decisions.reason: The day belongs to God because he brings it, as in 2:12 and 13:6, 9. The enemy's attack is his work.

decisions.choice: panic and trampling and confusion: three words that sound alike
decisions.reason: The three nouns share sounds and build a picture of a crowd in terror, as in Micah 7:4.

decisions.choice: breaking down the wall and crying out to the mountain
alternatives: a crying to the mountains for help
decisions.reason: Both phrases are rare and their sense is debated. The first may mean an enemy battering down walls; the second may be cries for help that echo off the hills, or the shout of the attackers. The words also sound like "Kir" and "shield" in verse 6.

decisions.choice: Enemies will break down / People will scream
decisions.reason: Readable supplies the subjects of the two actions, following the most likely sense.

records.source: וְעֵילָם֙ נָשָׂ֣א אַשְׁפָּ֔ה בְּרֶ֥כֶב אָדָ֖ם פָּֽרָשִׁ֑ים וְקִ֥יר עֵרָ֖ה מָגֵֽן׃
records.gloss: And Elam took up [the] quiver, with chariotry of men, horsemen, and Kir laid bare [the] shield.
pieces: Elam shouldered its quiver, with chariots, men and horsemen, \q and Kir stripped the cover from its shield.

L.6: And Elam took up [the] quiver, with chariots of men [and] horsemen, \q and Kir laid bare [the] shield.

R.6: Soldiers from Elam came with their arrows. They had chariots and horsemen. \q Soldiers from Kir got their shields ready for battle.

decisions.choice: Elam and Kir: peoples far to the east, serving in the attacking army
decisions.reason: Elam lay east of Babylonia; Kir is the place to which Assyria exiled the people of Damascus (2 Kings 16:9; Amos 1:5). Both supplied soldiers to the empires of Assyria and Babylon.

decisions.choice: chariots of men, horsemen: chariots with their crews and riders
decisions.reason: The phrase is compressed and may mean chariots manned by soldiers, together with cavalry.

decisions.choice: laid bare the shield: took off the shield's cover for battle
decisions.reason: Shields were kept in leather covers and uncovered before fighting.

decisions.choice: Soldiers from Elam / Soldiers from Kir
decisions.reason: Readable says that the place names stand for the soldiers they sent.

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י מִבְחַר־עֲמָקַ֖יִךְ מָ֣לְאוּ רָ֑כֶב וְהַפָּ֣רָשִׁ֔ים שֹׁ֖ת שָׁ֥תוּ הַשָּֽׁעְרָה׃
records.gloss: And it was, the choicest of your valleys were full of chariotry, and the horsemen took a firm stand at the gate.
pieces: Your finest valleys were filled with chariots, \q and horsemen took up their stations at the gates.

L.7: And it was [that] your choicest valleys were full of chariots, \q and the horsemen set themselves in position at the gate.

R.7: The best valleys around your city were full of enemy chariots. \q Horsemen took their places at the city gates.

decisions.choice: and it was: the prophet describes what he sees as already done
decisions.reason: The verbs of verses 7-8 are past forms. The prophet sees the coming attack as if it has happened, as visions often present the future.

decisions.choice: took a firm stand: set themselves in battle position
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. The cavalry is ready at the city gate.

decisions.choice: around your city / enemy chariots
decisions.reason: Readable says whose valleys and whose chariots.

records.source: וַיְגַ֕ל אֵ֖ת מָסַ֣ךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַתַּבֵּט֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא אֶל־נֶ֖שֶׁק בֵּ֥ית הַיָּֽעַר׃
records.gloss: And he uncovered the covering of Judah, and you looked in that day to [the] weaponry of [the] house of the forest.
pieces: Judah's covering was torn off, \q and on that day you turned your eyes to the weapons in the House of the Forest.

L.8: And [one] removed the covering of Judah, \q and you looked in that day to the weapons of the house of the forest.

R.8: Judah was left without protection. \q At that time you looked to the weapons stored in the House of the Forest.

decisions.choice: he uncovered: the subject is not named
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject. It may be the enemy, or God, who exposes Judah's weakness. The sentence is read here as describing what happened without naming who did it.

decisions.choice: the covering of Judah: Judah's protection
decisions.reason: The covering may be the fortresses that shielded Judah, or the veil that kept its leaders from seeing the danger.

decisions.choice: the house of the forest: Solomon's armory
decisions.reason: Solomon's House of the Forest of Lebanon was built with rows of cedar pillars, and shields of gold were kept in it (1 Kings 7:2; 10:17).

decisions.choice: was torn off / was left without protection
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a passive, which keeps the subject unnamed as the Hebrew does.

records.source: וְאֵ֨ת בְּקִיעֵ֧י עִיר־דָּוִ֛ד רְאִיתֶ֖ם כִּי־רָ֑בּוּ וַֽתְּקַבְּצ֔וּ אֶת־מֵ֥י הַבְּרֵכָ֖ה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And the breaches of [the] city of David you saw, that they were many, and you gathered the waters of the lower pool.
pieces: You saw how many breaches there were in the city of David, \q and you gathered in the water of the lower pool.

L.9: And the breaches of the city of David you saw, that they were many, \q and you collected the waters of the lower pool.

R.9: You saw that the walls of the city of David had many gaps. \q You stored up water from the lower pool.

decisions.choice: you gathered the waters of the lower pool: Hezekiah's preparation for siege
decisions.reason: Hezekiah stopped up the springs outside the city and brought water inside by a tunnel (2 Kings 20:20; 2 Chronicles 32:3-4, 30). Verses 9-11 list the defenses made ready against Assyria in 701 BC.

decisions.choice: the city of David: the old citadel of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The name was first given to the stronghold of Zion that David captured (2 Samuel 5:7, 9).

records.source: וְאֶת־בָּתֵּ֥י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם סְפַרְתֶּ֑ם וַתִּתְֿצוּ֙ הַבָּ֣תִּ֔ים לְבַצֵּ֖ר הַחוֹמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And the houses of Jerusalem you counted, and you pulled down the houses to fortify the wall.
pieces: You numbered the houses of Jerusalem \q and broke some of them down to make the wall stronger.

L.10: And the houses of Jerusalem you counted, \q and you pulled down the houses to fortify the wall.

R.10: You counted the houses in Jerusalem. \q Then you tore some of them down and used the stones to make the city wall stronger.

decisions.choice: counted the houses ... pulled down the houses: stones taken for the wall
decisions.reason: Houses were surveyed and some demolished to supply stone for repairing and thickening the wall (2 Chronicles 32:5). Remains of a thick wall from Hezekiah's time, built across older houses, have been found in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: used the stones
decisions.reason: Readable says how pulling down houses strengthened the wall.

records.source: וּמִקְוָ֣ה׀עֲשִׂיתֶ֗ם בֵּ֚ין הַחֹ֣מֹתַ֔יִם לְמֵ֖י הַבְּרֵכָ֣ה הַיְשָׁנָ֑ה וְלֹ֤א הִבַּטְתֶּם֙ אֶל־עֹשֶׂ֔יהָ וְיֹצְרָ֥הּ מֵֽרָח֖וֹק לֹ֥א רְאִיתֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And a reservoir you made between the two walls for [the] waters of the old pool, and not you looked to [the one who] made it, and [the one who] formed it from long ago not you saw.
pieces: Between the two walls you made a basin to hold the water of the old pool. \q But you never looked to its maker, \q or paid heed to the one who formed it long ago.

L.11: And a reservoir you made between the two walls \q for the waters of the old pool, \q but you did not look to [the one who] made it, \q and [the one who] formed it long ago you did not see.

R.11: You built a pool between the two walls to hold water from the old pool. \q But you did not turn to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who made all this happen. \q You paid no attention to the one who had it in mind long ago.

decisions.choice: you did not look to the one who made it: they trusted their defenses, not God
decisions.reason: "Looked" repeats the verb of verse 8: the people looked to weapons and water works but not to God. "Made" and "formed" are God's work, the same pair as in 37:26 (2 Kings 19:25), where God says he planned long ago what he now brings about.

decisions.choice: made it ... formed it: the city's coming disaster, or the city itself
alternatives: the one who made the pool
decisions.reason: The pronoun "it" is feminine. It may refer to the city and its water, which God made, or to the whole event God planned. Either way the one meant is God.

decisions.choice: the LORD, who made all this happen
decisions.reason: Readable names God, the one meant by "the one who made it", and follows the reading that "it" is the coming event.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא לִבְכִי֙ וּלְמִסְפֵּ֔ד וּלְקָרְחָ֖ה וְלַחֲגֹ֥ר שָֽׂק׃
records.gloss: And called [the] Lord Yahweh of hosts in that day for weeping and for mourning and for baldness and for girding [with] sackcloth.
pieces: On that day the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies called \q for weeping and lament, \q for shaved heads and for the wearing of sackcloth.

L.12: And the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of hosts called in that day \q for weeping and for mourning \q and for baldness and for putting on sackcloth.

R.12: At that time the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people to cry and mourn. \q He told them to shave their heads and wear rough clothes made of sackcloth.

decisions.choice: baldness ... sackcloth: signs of mourning and repentance
decisions.reason: People shaved their heads and wore rough sackcloth to grieve and to turn back to God (15:2-3; Joel 1:13; Micah 1:16).

decisions.choice: called for weeping: God summoned them to repent
decisions.reason: The danger was a call to humble themselves before God. Their answer is the feast of verse 13.

decisions.choice: called his people / He told them
decisions.reason: Readable says whom God called.

records.source: וְהִנֵּ֣ה׀שָׂשׂ֣וֹן וְשִׂמְחָ֗ה הָרֹ֤ג׀בָּקָר֙ וְשָׁחֹ֣ט צֹ֔אן אָכֹ֥ל בָּשָׂ֖ר וְשָׁת֣וֹת יָ֑יִן אָכ֣וֹל וְשָׁת֔וֹ כִּ֥י מָחָ֖ר נָמֽוּת׃
records.gloss: And look, joy and gladness, killing cattle and slaughtering sheep, eating meat and drinking wine: eating and drinking, for tomorrow we will die.
pieces: Instead, there was feasting and merriment, cattle killed and sheep butchered, \q meat eaten and wine poured. \q "Let us eat and drink," you said, "because tomorrow we will die!"

L.13: But look, joy and gladness, slaying cattle and butchering sheep, \q eating meat and drinking wine: \q "Eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!"

R.13: Instead, you laughed and celebrated. You killed cattle and sheep for feasts. \q You ate meat and drank wine. \q You said, "Let us eat and drink now, because tomorrow we will die!"

decisions.choice: killing ... eating ... drinking: a string of verbs without subjects
decisions.reason: The verbs are infinitives, which make a quick picture of a feast. The last pair is the people's own saying.

decisions.choice: let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die: quoted by Paul
decisions.reason: Paul quotes these words in 1 Corinthians 15:32 as the outlook of people who have no hope of resurrection.

decisions.choice: you said
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the last words as the people's own saying.

records.source: וְנִגְלָ֥ה בְאָזְנָ֖י יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת אִם־יְ֠כֻפַּר הֶעָוֺ֨ןהַזֶּ֤ה לָכֶם֙ עַד־תְּמֻת֔וּן אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃פ
records.gloss: And has revealed himself in my ears Yahweh of hosts: surely not will be atoned this iniquity for you until you die, says [the] Lord Yahweh of hosts.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has made {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} known to my ears: \q This guilt of yours will never be atoned for until the day you die, \q says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

L.14: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts revealed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} in my ears: \q Surely this iniquity will not be atoned for you until you die, \q says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of hosts.

R.14: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies spoke to me clearly. \q The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: \q This sin of yours will never be forgiven as long as you live.

decisions.choice: surely not: a solemn oath
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the form of an oath with the curse left unsaid ("if it will be atoned for ..."), which means "it will certainly not".

decisions.choice: atoned for: covered, wiped away
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for atonement (6:7). This sin of refusing to repent will not be removed while they live.

decisions.choice: until you die: for the rest of your lives
decisions.reason: The phrase answers the people's "tomorrow we will die" in verse 13. It does not say what happens after death.

decisions.choice: will never be forgiven as long as you live
decisions.reason: Readable says what "not be atoned for until you die" means.

records.source: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָא֑וֹת לֶךְ־בֹּא֙ אֶל־הַסֹּכֵ֣ן הַזֶּ֔ה עַל־שֶׁבְנָ֖א אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־הַבָּֽיִת׃
records.gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh of hosts: come, go to this steward, to Shebna, who [is] over the house:
pieces: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: \q "Go to this steward, \q to Shebna, who is in charge of the palace, and say to him,

L.15: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of hosts: \q "Come, go to this steward, \q to Shebna, who [is] over the house, [and say,]

R.15: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: \q "Go to that official Shebna, the man in charge of the king's palace. Tell him,

decisions.choice: steward ... over the house: the chief official of the royal palace
decisions.reason: The man "over the house" managed the king's household and spoke for him (1 Kings 4:6; 2 Kings 15:5). In 36:3 and 2 Kings 18:18 Eliakim holds that office and Shebna is secretary, which suggests the change foretold here took place.

decisions.choice: this steward: said with contempt
decisions.reason: "This" points at Shebna with scorn, as the questions in verse 16 do. Shebna's father is not named, unlike Eliakim's (verse 20).

decisions.choice: and say
decisions.reason: The Hebrew moves straight into the message of verse 16; the words that introduce it are supplied.

records.heading: Shebna and Eliakim

records.source: מַה־לְּךָ֥ פֹה֙ וּמִ֣י לְךָ֣ פֹ֔ה כִּֽי־חָצַ֧בְתָּ לְּךָ֛ פֹּ֖ה קָ֑בֶר חֹצְבִ֤י מָרוֹם֙ קִבְר֔וֹ חֹקְקִ֥י בַסֶּ֖לַע מִשְׁכָּ֥ן לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: What [is] to you here, and who [is] to you here, that you have cut out for yourself here a tomb? Cutting out on high his tomb, carving in the rock a dwelling for himself!
pieces: 'What right do you have here, and who are your relatives here, \q that you have hewn a tomb for yourself here? \q He carves his grave high on the hill \q and hollows out a home for himself in the rock!

L.16: 'What [is] yours here, and whom [have] you here, \q that you have cut out a tomb for yourself here, \q cutting out his tomb on the height, \q carving a dwelling for himself in the rock?

R.16: 'What is yours here? \q Who said you could carve out a tomb for yourself in this place? \q You have made a fine tomb high up on the hill. \q You have carved a place for yourself in the rock to lie in when you die.

decisions.choice: a tomb ... a dwelling in the rock: a grand rock-cut tomb
decisions.reason: Wealthy families in Jerusalem cut tombs into the rock. Shebna prepares a lasting monument for himself, but verse 18 says he will die in a foreign land.

decisions.choice: what ... who: what claim and what family do you have here
decisions.reason: The questions ask what right Shebna has to a tomb in this place; he may have had no ancestral family there.

decisions.choice: cutting out ... carving: a sudden change to "he"
decisions.reason: The speech turns from "you" to "he", as if the prophet points Shebna out to others.

decisions.choice: You have made ... You have carved
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "you" throughout so the reader does not lose track of the person meant.

records.source: הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ מְטַלְטֶלְךָ֔ טַלְטֵלָ֖ה גָּ֑בֶר וְעֹטְךָ֖ עָטֹֽה׃
records.gloss: Look, Yahweh [is] about to hurl you, hurling, O man, and to grasp you firmly.
pieces: Look out, you strong man! \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is going to fling you far away \q and grip you hard.

L.17: Look, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is about to hurl you away, a hurling, O man, \q and to grasp you firmly.

R.17: You think you are such an important man. \q But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is about to grab you and throw you far away.

decisions.choice: O man: a mighty man, spoken in mockery
decisions.reason: The word means a strong man or warrior. Here it mocks Shebna's self-importance.

decisions.choice: grasp you firmly: seize you tightly
decisions.reason: The verb may instead mean "wrap" or "cover", taking hold of Shebna before winding him up in verse 18.

decisions.choice: You think you are such an important man
decisions.reason: Readable explains the mockery in "O man".

records.source: צָנ֤וֹף יִצְנָפְךָ֙ צְנֵפָ֔ה כַּדּ֕וּר אֶל־אֶ֖רֶץ רַחֲבַ֣ת יָדָ֑יִם שָׁ֣מָּה תָמ֗וּת וְשָׁ֨מָּה֙ מַרְכְּב֣וֹת כְּבוֹדֶ֔ךָ קְל֖וֹן בֵּ֥ית אֲדֹנֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Winding he will wind you [in] a winding, like a ball, to a land broad of both sides; there you will die, and there the chariots of your glory, O disgrace of [the] house of your master.
pieces: He will wind you round and round and fling you like a ball \q into a broad, open country. \q There you will die, and there your splendid chariots will stay, \q you disgrace to your master's house!

L.18: He will wind you up tightly, winding [you] like a ball, \q into a land wide on both sides. \q There you will die, and there [will be] the chariots of your glory, \q you disgrace to the house of your master!

R.18: He will wind you up like a ball and throw you far away into a wide open land. \q There you will die. There your fine chariots will be left. \q You have brought shame on your master, the king.

decisions.choice: a land broad of both sides: a wide, open country
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures a broad plain, like Mesopotamia, where a ball thrown far rolls on and on. Shebna will die in exile.

decisions.choice: the chariots of your glory: your splendid chariots
decisions.reason: The word usually rendered glory here means splendor or honor, the status Shebna displayed in his chariots.

decisions.choice: your master: the king
decisions.reason: The form is plural, a plural of majesty for Shebna's lord, the king of Judah (Hezekiah, 36:1-3).

decisions.choice: splendid chariots / fine chariots
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "glory"; Balanced and Readable say what it means here.

decisions.choice: the king
decisions.reason: Readable names Shebna's master.

records.source: וַהֲדַפְתִּ֖יךָ מִמַּצָּבֶ֑ךָ וּמִמַּעֲמָֽדְךָ֖ יֶהֶרְסֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And I will push you from your office, and from your position he will tear you down.
pieces: I will drive you out of your office, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will pull you down from your post.

L.19: And I will push you from your office, \q and from your position {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will pull you down.

R.19: I will remove you from your job. \q You will be thrown down from your high position.

decisions.choice: I ... he: God speaks first of himself, then of himself as "he"
decisions.reason: The change of person is common in prophetic speech. Both verbs have God as their subject.

decisions.choice: office ... position: Shebna's post at court
decisions.reason: The second word means a place where one stands, here a standing at court.

decisions.choice: You will be thrown down
decisions.reason: Readable uses a passive to avoid the confusing change from "I" to "he".

records.source: וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וְקָרָ֣אתִי לְעַבְדִּ֔י לְאֶלְיָקִ֖ים בֶּן־חִלְקִיָּֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And it will be in that day, and I will call my servant, Eliakim [the] son of Hilkiah.
pieces: When that day comes, I will call for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah.

L.20: And it will be in that day [that] I will call {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, Eliakim son of Hilkiah.

R.20: At that time I will call {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah.

decisions.choice: my servant: a title of honor for one God chooses
decisions.reason: God gives the title to David (37:35) and to Isaiah (20:3). It sets Eliakim, chosen by God, against Shebna, who served himself.

decisions.choice: Eliakim son of Hilkiah
decisions.reason: Eliakim is over the palace in 36:3, 22 and 37:2 (2 Kings 18:18), during Sennacherib's siege in 701 BC.

records.source: וְהִלְבַּשְׁתִּ֣יו כֻּתָּנְתֶּ֗ךָ וְאַבְנֵֽטְךָ֙ אֲחַזְּקֶ֔נּוּ וּמֶֽמְשֶׁלְתְּךָ֖אֶתֵּ֣ן בְּיָד֑וֹ וְהָיָ֥ה לְאָ֛ב לְיוֹשֵׁ֥ב יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וּלְבֵ֥ית יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I will clothe him [with] your tunic, and [with] your sash I will bind him, and your authority I will put in his hand, and he will become a father to [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem and to [the] house of Judah.
pieces: I will dress him in your robe and bind your sash on him. I will place your authority in his hand, and he will be a father to the people of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.

L.21: And I will clothe him [with] your robe, and [with] your sash I will bind him, and your authority I will put in his hand, and he will be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.

R.21: I will put your robe and your belt on him. I will give him your power. He will take care of the people of Jerusalem and Judah like a father.

decisions.choice: your tunic ... your sash: the robes of office
decisions.reason: The robe and sash marked the official's rank. Taking them from Shebna and putting them on Eliakim transfers the office (compare Numbers 20:26-28).

decisions.choice: a father: a protector and provider
decisions.reason: A father to the people is one who cares for them (Job 29:16), unlike Shebna, who cared for his own fame.

records.source: וְנָתַתִּ֛י מַפְתֵּ֥חַ בֵּית־דָּוִ֖ד עַל־שִׁכְמ֑וֹ וּפָתַח֙ וְאֵ֣ין סֹגֵ֔ר וְסָגַ֖ר וְאֵ֥ין פֹּתֵֽחַ׃
records.gloss: And I will put [the] key of [the] house of David on his shoulder, and he will open, and there is not [one who] shuts, and he will shut, and there is not [one who] opens.
pieces: I will lay the key of the house of David on his shoulder. When he opens, no one will close; when he closes, no one will open.

L.22: And I will put the key of the house of David on his shoulder, and he will open, and there [will be] none shutting, and he will shut, and there [will be] none opening.

R.22: I will give him the key to the palace of David's family. He will have the power to open doors that no one can close. He will close doors that no one can open.

decisions.choice: the key ... on his shoulder: the sign of authority over the palace
decisions.reason: The steward held the keys of the royal house and decided who could come in. A large key may have been carried on the shoulder, or the phrase pictures the weight of the office (9:5).

decisions.choice: the key of David: applied to Christ
decisions.reason: Revelation 3:7 takes up these words for the risen Christ, who "has the key of David" and opens what no one can shut.

decisions.choice: the power to ... doors
decisions.reason: Readable says that opening and shutting picture full authority over the palace.

records.source: וּתְקַעְתִּ֥יו יָתֵ֖ד בְּמָק֣וֹם נֶאֱמָ֑ן וְהָיָ֛ה לְכִסֵּ֥א כָב֖וֹד לְבֵ֥ית אָבִֽיו׃
records.gloss: And I will drive him [as] a peg in a place firm, and he will become a seat of honor for [the] house of his father.
pieces: I will drive him in like a peg where the ground holds fast, and he will be a seat of honor for his father's house.

L.23: And I will drive him [like] a peg into a firm place, and he will become a throne of honor for the house of his father.

R.23: I will make him firm, like a tent peg hammered into solid ground. He will bring honor to his father's family.

decisions.choice: a peg in a firm place: something fixed and dependable
decisions.reason: A peg could be a tent stake or a peg in a wall for hanging things (verse 24). It pictures a secure leader (Ezra 9:8; Zechariah 10:4).

decisions.choice: a seat of honor: a source of honor
decisions.reason: The word for seat is also the word for a throne. Eliakim's rise will bring honor to his family.

decisions.choice: seat of honor / bring honor
decisions.reason: The word often rendered glory here means honor or importance; Literal keeps "throne of honor", Balanced "seat of honor".

records.source: וְתָל֨וּ עָלָ֜יו כֹּ֣ל׀כְּב֣וֹד בֵּית־אָבִ֗יו הַצֶּֽאֱצָאִים֙ וְהַצְּפִע֔וֹת כֹּ֖ל כְּלֵ֣י הַקָּטָ֑ן מִכְּלֵי֙ הָֽאַגָּנ֔וֹת וְעַ֖ד כָּל־כְּלֵ֥י הַנְּבָלִֽים׃
records.gloss: And they will hang on him all [the] weight of [the] house of his father, the offspring and the offshoots, all the vessels of the small, from vessels of bowls to all vessels of jars.
pieces: They will hang on him the whole weight of his father's family, its children and its descendants, every small vessel, from basins to every storage jar.

L.24: And they will hang on him all the weight of the house of his father, the offspring and the shoots, all the small vessels, from the vessels of bowls to all the vessels of jars.

R.24: His whole family will depend on him, like pots and jars hanging from a peg. All his relatives and their children will rely on him, from the least important to the greatest.

decisions.choice: weight: the glory or burden of the family
decisions.reason: The word means both "weight" and "honor". The family's honor, and its full weight, will hang on Eliakim like pots on a peg.

decisions.choice: the offspring and the shoots: all the family's descendants
decisions.reason: The two words picture shoots coming out from a plant; the second appears only here. The relatives crowd onto Eliakim for favor.

decisions.choice: small vessels, bowls, jars: household pots and storage jars
decisions.reason: The image is of every kind of vessel hung on one peg, from small bowls to large jars.

decisions.choice: from the least important to the greatest
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of vessels of every size.

records.source: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא נְאֻם֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת תָּמוּשׁ֙ הַיָּתֵ֔ד הַתְּקוּעָ֖ה בְּמָק֣וֹם נֶאֱמָ֑ן וְנִגְדְּעָ֣ה וְנָפְלָ֗ה וְנִכְרַת֙ הַמַּשָּׂ֣א אֲשֶׁר־עָלֶ֔יהָ כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃ס
records.gloss: In that day, declares Yahweh of hosts, will give way the peg driven in a place firm, and it will be cut down and will fall, and will be cut off the burden which [was] on it, for Yahweh has spoken.
pieces: On that day, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the peg fixed in a secure place will work loose. It will be hacked off and fall, and everything it held will be cut away, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken.'"

L.25: In that day, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the peg that was driven into a firm place will be removed, and it will be cut down and fall, and the load that [was] on it will be cut off, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken.'"

R.25: At that time, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the peg that was hammered into solid ground will come loose. It will break and fall. Everything hanging on it will crash down. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has said it.'"

decisions.choice: the peg: Eliakim, who was made secure in verse 23
decisions.reason: The words repeat verse 23, so the peg is most likely Eliakim, who falls under the weight of his family's demands (verse 24). Others take it to be Shebna, the subject of verses 15-19.

decisions.choice: the burden: the load on the peg, a play on "oracle"
decisions.reason: The word is the same as "oracle" in verse 1. The chapter that began with a burden from God ends with the burden falling.

decisions.choice: Everything hanging on it
decisions.reason: Readable says what the load is: the family that hung on the peg in verse 24.
